authors: Tuukka Korhonen (University of Bergen, Norway), Konrad Majewski (University of Warsaw, Norway), Wojciech Nadara (University of Warsaw, Norway), Michał Pilipczuk (University of Warsaw, Norway), Marek Sokołowski (University of Warsaw, Norway)
statement: III. C ONCLUSIONS We presented a data structure for the dynamic treewidth problem that achieves amortized update time √ 2Ok ( log n log log n) . The obvious open question is to improve this complexity. It is plausible that some optimization √ of the current approach could result in shaving off the log√log n factor in the exponent, but complexity of the form 2Ok ( log n) seems inherent to the recursive approach we use. Nevertheless, we conjecture that it should be possible to achieve update time that is polylogarithmic in n for every fixed k, that is, of the form logOk (1) n, or maybe even Ok (logc n) for some universal constant c. The ultimate goal would be to get closer to the O(log n) bound achieved by Bodlaender for the case k = 2 [22]. Apart from the above, we hope that our result may open new directions in the design of parameterized dynamic data structures. More precisely, dynamic programming on tree decompositions is used as a building block in multiple different techniques in algorithm design, so Theorem I.1 may be useful for designing dynamic counterparts of those techniques. Here is list some possible directions.
context: Theorem I.1 could be applied in combination with metakernelization to obtain data structures for maintaining small kernels in dynamic graphs. D OMINATING S ET on planar graphs would probably be the first problem to look into, as it admits a simple kernelization algorithms that predates (and inspired) meta-kernelization [49]. We remark that dynamic kernelization has already been studied as a way to obtain dynamic parameterized data structures [24], [36]. • III.
